changes.before: Define EachList<T> distributively. names must hold Oak and Elm, counts must hold 2 and 7.
changes.after: Apply a type choice to each member of a union separately.

before: When a conditional checks a bare type parameter T, a union input is considered one member at a time. EachList<T> uses T extends unknown, a condition that accepts every ordinary member here, to produce an array for each member separately. unknown is the broad safe type; never contributes no possible member.

EachList<string | number> becomes string[] | number[], not (string | number)[]. The first allows an all-string array or an all-number array. A mixed array is not assignable to either member. No arrays are created by this type alias; the example writes the arrays explicitly and prints their lengths, 2 and 2.
Optional local practice: Compare an explicitly typed (string | number)[] containing both kinds with the union of arrays.
after: When a conditional type checks T directly, it can apply to each member of a union separately. This is called distribution. Here, string becomes string[] and number becomes number[].
EachList<string | number> becomes string[] or number[]. That means an all-text list or an all-number list. The type does not create either list for you.
`(string | number)[]` means something different: each item can be text or a number, so one list can mix both kinds.
A list containing Map and 3 does not fit EachList<string | number>. It is neither all text nor all numbers.
